content.name: p
children: Use pgroles as the PostgreSQL access-control layer next to your existing application and schema lifecycle.

content.name: p
children: Most stacks already have a way to create tables, indexes, functions, and application metadata. Keep that path responsible for schema DDL. Let pgroles own PostgreSQL roles, memberships, grants, default privileges, passwords, and retirements.

content.name: p
children: pgroles is intentionally not a schema migration framework. It does not create tables, rewrite indexes, manage row-level security policies, or replace application migration history.

children.name: td

children.name: td

children.name: td

content.name: p
children: This avoids the common failure mode where application bootstrap scripts, deployment jobs, and operators all issue their own

content.name: p
children: For each environment, converge access control after the database exists and before application traffic relies on new privileges:

content.name: Fence
children:
# 1. Apply schema changes with the service's schema-owner role.
./service-migrate

# 2. Preview and apply role and privilege policy.
pgroles diff -f pgroles.yaml --database-url "$DATABASE_URL"
pgroles apply -f pgroles.yaml --database-url "$DATABASE_URL"

# 3. Deploy or restart application workloads.

content.name: p
children: If schema changes create new objects in an already-managed schema, pgroles has two safety nets:

children.name: li
children: wildcard grants cover objects that already exist when pgroles runs

children.name: li
children: default privileges cover future objects created by the configured owner

content.name: p
children: If schema changes need a brand-new schema, either declare that schema in pgroles so pgroles creates it and converges its PostgreSQL owner, or create the schema first and then apply the pgroles policy that grants access to it.

content.name: p
children: Prefer separate roles for distinct duties:

children.name: td
children: Runs schema changes and owns created objects

children.name: td
children: Grants human access through membership rather than direct grants

children.name: td
children: Runs pgroles with enough authority to converge the declared policy

content.name: p
children: This makes privilege boundaries visible in one manifest instead of scattering them across connection strings and setup scripts.

content.name: p
children: Some PostgreSQL-backed libraries and platform features create their own tables, functions, triggers, queues, publications, or metadata schemas. Treat those as schema-owned systems:

children.name: li
children: give the owner or installer role enough privilege to create and upgrade its own objects

children.name: li
children: let that owner path create or upgrade the schema objects

children.name: li
children: use pgroles to grant narrower runtime and team roles access to the resulting objects

children.name: li
children: include default privileges for the owner/schema pair if future upgrades create more tables, sequences, or functions

content.name: p
children: Do not point pgroles at an internally managed schema and expect it to understand that system's upgrade invariants. pgroles manages privileges around those objects; the schema-owning system still owns its DDL.

content.name: p
children: If the owner role is also managed by pgroles in
mode, declare the privileges that role should keep on its own schema. PostgreSQL owners effectively have broad access to their objects, and pgroles treats undeclared visible privileges as drift.

content.name: p
children: For one application, a single manifest is often enough. For a shared database with multiple teams, use bundle mode so each team owns a scoped fragment:

content.name: Fence
children:
pgroles validate --bundle pgroles.bundle.yaml
pgroles diff --bundle pgroles.bundle.yaml --database-url "$DATABASE_URL"
pgroles apply --bundle pgroles.bundle.yaml --database-url "$DATABASE_URL"

content.name: p
children: Bundle composition gives each fragment an explicit ownership boundary. If two fragments both try to manage the same role, schema facet, grant, default privilege, or membership selector, pgroles rejects the bundle before it connects to PostgreSQL.

content.name: p
